To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
labelling plays a positive role within the perceived control dimension of the Reasoned Action approach (RAA) as well as on attitudes in influencing behavioural intention to purchase.
Labelling has a positive influence on consumers' perceived behavioral control, which in turn positively affects consumers' intention to buy organic products.
the more that respondents agree labelling is actionable the more positive their attitudes, sense of control and hence intention and behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how information influences consumer behaviour, and the role of information in facilitating consumer decision making.
the role of labelling to increase consumer confidence in organic products and thereby increase the consumption of organic food.
the role of labelling in the consumption of organic food.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the more that consumers agree that labelling of organic products is actionable, the greater the perceived behavioural control, the more positive the attitude, the more likely the behavioural intention and hence the more likely the behaviour.
labelling plays a positive role on the RAA dimensions and hence behavioural intention.
labelling is an important component of the RAA in the organic food domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more actionable information that is provided to consumers, the more positive the attitude and sense of behavioural control, and the stronger the intention and (self-reported) behaviour.
labelling is an actionable information source that can be used to influence consumers' perceptions and hence their behaviour.
labelling is an important tool to increase consumers' perceived behavioural controls and hence intention to purchase organic foods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
labelling can have a direct effect on consumers' intention to purchase organic products, and that this effect is mediated by perceived control over the purchase decision.
labelling can be an effective tool to influence consumer behaviour and increase the consumption of sustainable food products.
labelling is a key tool to help consumers make better food choices and that labelling should include actionable information.
